name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |

          cd web

      - name: Verify tag and synchronized versions
        run: |
          PACKAGE_VERSION="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          TAG_VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          test "${TAG_VERSION}" = "${PACKAGE_VERSION}"
          bun scripts/sync-version.ts --check

      - name: Test and build
        run: |
          bun run build
          bun test ./test/*.test.ts
          cd web
          bun test

      - name: Verify npm package contents
        run: |
          npm pack --ignore-scripts --dry-run --json > npm-pack.json
          node scripts/verify-package-manifest.mjs npm-pack.json

  build:
    needs: validate
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            arch: x64
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: linux
            arch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
          - os: darwin
            arch: x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
          - os: darwin
            arch: arm64
            runner: macos-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.13

      - name: Build
        run: |
          bun install --frozen-lockfile
          bun scripts/sync-version.ts --check
          bun x tsc -p tsconfig.json
          bun scripts/copy-core-templates.ts

      - name: Create bundle
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}"
          BUNDLE_NAME="keating-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          STAGE_DIR="${BUNDLE_NAME}"
          mkdir -p "${STAGE_DIR}"
          mkdir -p "${STAGE_DIR}/bin"
          cp bin/keating.js "${STAGE_DIR}/bin/"
          cp -r dist pi scripts/install "${STAGE_DIR}/"
          cp package.json "${STAGE_DIR}/"
          # Bundle node_modules so the tarball is truly standalone
          cp -r node_modules "${STAGE_DIR}/"
          mv "${STAGE_DIR}/install/install.sh" "${STAGE_DIR}/install.sh"
          rm -rf "${STAGE_DIR}/install"
          tar -czf "${BUNDLE_NAME}.tar.gz" "${STAGE_DIR}"

      - name: Verify bundle contents
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}"
          BUNDLE_NAME="keating-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"

          grep -Fx "${BUNDLE_NAME}/dist/src/pi/hyper-teacher/index.js" bundle-files.txt
          ! grep -F "${BUNDLE_NAME}/bin/.keating/" bundle-files.txt
          ! grep -F "${BUNDLE_NAME}/bin/keating.config.json" bundle-files.txt

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: keating-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: keating-*.tar.gz

  release:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: artifacts

      - name: Create release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: artifacts/**/*.tar.gz
          generate_release_notes: true

  publish-npm:
    needs: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Setup Node for npm trusted publishing
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.13

      - name: Build
        run: |
          bun install --frozen-lockfile
          cd web
          bun install --frozen-lockfile
          cd ..
          bun run build

      - name: Publish to npm
        run: |
          npm pack --ignore-scripts --dry-run --json > npm-pack.json
          node scripts/verify-package-manifest.mjs npm-pack.json
          npm publish --ignore-scripts --provenance --access public

result.output:
**isomorphic-git** is "a pure JavaScript reimplementation of git that works in both Node.js and browser JavaScript environments." It reads and writes git repositories and can fetch from and push to remotes like GitHub, "all without any native C++ module dependencies."

**Key features**

- Aims for "100% interoperability with the canonical git implementation," working by modifying files in a `.git` directory just as regular git does.
- Ships with a CLI called `isogit`, described as "a thin shell that translates command line arguments into the equivalent JS API commands."
- Designed for modern bundlers — the API is "designed with modern tools like Rollup and Webpack in mind," and exposing individual functions lets bundlers "produce smaller bundles by including only the functions your application uses."
- Includes TypeScript type definitions for static type-checking and editor autocompletion.
- Follows semantic versioning; breaking changes only on major bumps.

**Browser / environment support** (tested in CI): Node 10, Chrome 79, Edge 79, Firefox 72, Safari 13, Android 10, iOS 13.

**Filesystem and HTTP requirements**

Because browsers lack an `fs` module and HTTP APIs differ between platforms, the library "lets you bring your own file system and HTTP client." In Node you pass the native `fs` plus `isomorphic-git/http/node`; in the browser you supply an `fs`-API emulator plus `isomorphic-git/http/web`. The recommended browser option is LightningFS ("the easiest to setup and most performant library"), maintained by the same author; ZenFS and Filer are also listed as compatible. One caveat noted: LightningFS "may apply file operations out of order, which can lead to repository corruption if the process crashes" — mitigated by calling `fs.flush()`.

**Supported operations** — clone, push, pull, fetch, commit, branch, checkout, log, walk, merge, status, statusMatrix, add, remove, stash, tag, and low-level read/write object commands (readBlob, readCommit, readTree, writeTree, etc.). Note: there is **no `diff` command** in the listed API; `walk` and `statusMatrix` are the closest equivalents.

**CORS**: due to same-origin policy, browser usage generally needs a proxy — `@isomorphic-git/cors-proxy`, a CloudFlare worker, or the free `https://cors.isomorphic-git.org`. Gogs, Gitea, and Azure DevOps support CORS; GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket do not.

**Two things you asked about that aren't in this page:**

- **Bundle size** — no figures are given anywhere in the README.
- **IndexedDB** — never mentioned explicitly. Browser use is supported via a pluggable `fs` layer; LightningFS's storage backend isn't described here.

Also worth noting on project health: the original author left, and it's now maintained by two volunteers (@jcubic, @mojavelinux) who "don't write much code, mainly do code review and try to answer to issues." Licensed MIT; 8.3k stars, 483 forks.

Replace the internals of `lix-sandbox.ts` behind its existing exported API (`lixCommit`, `lixListBranches`, `lixDiffCommits`, …) so `SandboxView.tsx` doesn't change. That keeps it a contained swap and gets you real history. Treat GitHub sync as a separate, later call because of the CORS proxy.

# Swap the sandbox VC engine to isomorphic-git

## Context

`web/src/keating/lix-sandbox.ts` is a 370-line hand-rolled IndexedDB store written as a
placeholder. Its own header says it exists only because `@lix-js/sdk` needs native Node
addons and can't run in the browser, and that it should be swapped out when a browser-capable
option appears. isomorphic-git is that option.

Beyond the naming, the placeholder has three real defects that a swap fixes:

1. **It stores hashes, not content.** `lixCommit` (`lix-sandbox.ts:200`) computes a
   `contentHash` per path and discards the file body. So `lixDiffCommits` (`:292`) can report
   *that* a file changed but never *what*, and there is no restore path at all — nothing was
   kept to restore from.
2. **Branching is cosmetic.** `lixCommit` calls `ensureMainBranch()` and writes to `main.id`
   unconditionally, ignoring the active branch. `lixSwitchBranch` (`:284`) sets a
   `localStorage` key that `lixCommit` never reads. Create a branch, commit, and it lands on
   main.
3. **`@lix-js/sdk` is a dead dependency** — declared in `package.json:77` and
   `web/package.json:53`, imported nowhere in the repo.

Outcome: real content-addressed history with working branches, restore into the sandbox, and
naming that matches the engine.

## Decisions taken

- Old history is **dropped**. It cannot be faithfully migrated — the blobs were never stored.
  v1 portable bundles are rejected with an explicit message.
- **Restore-to-sandbox is in scope**, since storing content is what makes it possible.
- No remote operations (clone/push/pull). That avoids the CORS-proxy problem entirely —
  GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket don't send CORS headers. Local repo only.

## Approach

### New module: `web/src/keating/sandbox-git.ts` (replaces `lix-sandbox.ts`)

Export a `createSandboxGit({ fs, dir })` factory, with module-level functions delegating to a
lazily-created default instance backed by LightningFS. The injectable `fs` is what makes this
testable — the current module is untested because it can only talk to browser IndexedDB.

Git is a **side-car history**, not the live filesystem: nodepod stays the source of truth for
sandbox files, exactly as today. `sandboxCommit` receives files from
`nodePodGetAllFileContents()` (`nodepod-runtime.ts:418`), writes them into the git worktree,
stages, and commits.

| Current | New | Implementation |

Done. The swap is committed on `main` (not pushed — say the word and I'll push).

## What changed

`web/src/keating/lix-sandbox.ts` → `web/src/keating/sandbox-git.ts`, backed by isomorphic-git over LightningFS. Names follow the engine: `lixCommit`→`sandboxCommit`, `lixSwitchBranch`→`sandboxCheckoutBranch`, `getSandboxLix`→`getSandboxRepo`, `SandboxVcExport`→`SandboxGitExport`. Call sites updated in `SandboxView.tsx`, `sandbox-export.ts`, `nodepod-runtime.ts`, and `export.ts`.

Both defects from the old implementation are gone: history now retains real content (so diffs are backed by real blobs), and commits land on the checked-out branch instead of always on main. Added the restore action — a **Restore** button per commit that writes that commit's files back into the nodepod sandbox.

Dropped `@lix-js/sdk` from both manifests.

## Two things worth your attention

**A bug I found by testing the right seam.** My first 8 tests ran the engine over node's `fs` — they passed immediately, which was suspicious, because they don't exercise the actual browser backing store. So I added a second suite driving real LightningFS over a fake IndexedDB. It failed instantly: LightningFS's top-level `flush()` is callback-based, and I'd been calling it as a promise. That threw on **every commit in the browser** while all node-fs tests stayed green. Fixed to use `promises.flush()`. Both suites now pass.

**I couldn't do the manual browser pass.** The plan called for clicking through the Sandbox VC tab, but the Chrome extension isn't connected — `tabs_context_mcp` reports it unavailable. I didn't retry past that. The LightningFS suite covers the browser-storage seam that manual testing would mostly have been checking, but nobody has yet watched the actual UI: the Restore button, the branch list, the diff panel. That's the gap.

One deliberate scope call: no remote operations (clone/push/pull), which is what keeps the CORS-proxy problem out of this change. Pushing the sandbox to a real GitHub repo remains a separate project.
